questions.prompt: The general will lead the soldiers through the mountains, and they will save the city.
questions.answer: ὁ στρατηγὸς τοὺς στρατιώτας διὰ τῶν ὀρῶν ἄξει, καὶ τὴν πόλιν σώσουσιν.

questions.prompt: Those who fight bravely will receive a great reward from the king.
questions.answer: οἱ ἀνδρείως ἀγωνιζόμενοι μέγα ἆθλον παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως λήψονται.

questions.prompt: When the enemy have crossed the river, we shall no longer be safe.

questions.prompt: I know that the citizens will bear these misfortunes with difficulty.

questions.prompt: What shall we say to the judges about these things?

questions.prompt: Shall we remain here, or shall we flee to the sea?

questions.prompt: Whom shall I trust, now that my friends have betrayed me?

questions.prompt: How shall we escape the danger that threatens the city?
questions.answer: πῶς τὸν κίνδυνον τὸν τῇ πόλει ἐπικείμενον φευξόμεθα;

questions.prompt: You will read the law aloud to the assembled citizens.
questions.answer: ἀναγνώσει μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ τὸν νόμον τοῖς συνειλεγμένοις πολίταις.

questions.prompt: If you are wise, you will spare yourselves and not the tyrant.

questions.prompt: Will you not cease from your anger and listen to your friends?

questions.prompt: See to it that you prove yourselves worthy of your ancestors.
questions.answer: ὅπως ἄξιοι τῶν προγόνων ἔσεσθε.

questions.prompt: Take care that you say nothing shameful before the people.
questions.answer: ὅπως μηδὲν αἰσχρὸν ἐν τῷ δήμῳ ἐρεῖς.

questions.prompt: A reasonable man will bear his misfortunes more easily than the foolish.

questions.answer: ὁ χάριν εἰδὼς οὐδέποτε τῶν εὖ ποιησάντων ἐπιλήσεται.

questions.prompt: Whoever trusts a flatterer will quickly repent.
questions.answer: ὅστις κόλακι πιστεύσει, ταχέως μεταμελήσει αὐτῷ.
